finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a filename that includes shell metacharacters or control operators, leading to command injection.
finding.assumptions: The filename is directly passed to the open function without any validation or sanitization.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the sink is std::ofstream::open, which opens a file directly via the OS file API and does not invoke a shell or execute a command string. No command-line parsing or shell invocation occurs, so shell metacharacters in the filename cannot lead to command injection. No additional checks are required for this operation.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a message that includes shell metacharacters or control operators, leading to command injection.
finding.assumptions: The message is directly output to the log file or standard output without any validation or sanitization.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The sink is a stream insertion operator (output << message) which writes to a file or stdout; it does not invoke any shell or system call. No path exists from the untrusted source to a command execution primitive. Therefore, the reported OS Command Injection cannot occur.
